Variants.Content: House Hornwood is a northern vassal sworn to House Stark, rooted in Hornwood and its surrounding forests, valleys, and farmlands, with a brown bull moose on an orange field as its sigil. With its lands wedged between stronger neighbors such as Manderly and Bolton, the family's importance comes not from grand royal legends, but from land, succession, and its position along the roads. Northern nobles know that once succession grows uncertain in what seems an ordinary middling house, marriage pacts, wardships, and neighboring ambitions will immediately turn a private matter into regional politics.

When the lords of the North look upon the Hornwood lands, what they see first is often not the bull moose sigil, but its position wedged between several powerful neighbors. Forests, stream valleys, and farmlands are enough to sustain a respectable house, and also enough to invite scheming over marriages, wardships, and inheritance. Whether House Hornwood can keep its own name often depends on whether kinship ties prove stronger than its neighbors' appetites.

The farmers of the Hornwood lands know the trouble of moose trampling fences, and they know that when great folk argue over succession, smallfolk worry first about who will collect next season's rent. To them, whether the sigil changes masters matters far less than who holds timber rights, the mill, and the winter grain; yet so long as the Hornwood banner flies, old custom still has a name that can be spoken clearly.
